title: One-pass normalizer
goal:
Implement Algorithm 3 (lines 1-6) from the paper. Write `online_normalizer(xs)`, which reads `xs` exactly once, from left to right, and returns `(m, d)`: the maximum $m_V$ and the normalizer $d_V = \sum_j e^{x_j - m_V}$.

The tests pass `xs` as a one-shot iterator, so a second pass over the input finds nothing. The starter includes a finished `online_softmax` that calls your function and then runs the second pass of Algorithm 3 (lines 7-9).
hints: Start from $m_0 = -\infty$ and $d_0 = 0$. `math.inf` and `-math.inf` are fine inputs to `math.exp`: `math.exp(-math.inf)` is `0.0`, which makes the first step work without a special case.
On each element, compute the new maximum first. Then $d_j = d_{j-1} e^{m_{j-1} - m_j} + e^{x_j - m_j}$ (Algorithm 3, line 5). Both exponents are at most 0.
Don't call `max(xs)` before the loop. That is the first pass of safe softmax, and it uses up the iterator.
